<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Scan contents and seal a Package for a Pack task's order"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/tasks/{id}/seal-package"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



The Pack-path counterpart to `complete`: the station holding the active claim on a Pack task scans the order's contents and seals them into a brand-new Package resource (created by this call, not pre-existing — see the `Location` header). The task itself is left claimed; a separate `POST /tasks/{id}/complete` call finishes the Pack task once the package is sealed. Requires at least one scanned item — an empty `contents` array is a domain invariant violation (`422`), not a malformed request (`400`), since the array is present and well-formed, just semantically insufficient to seal.

**Ship in own container (opt-in, [ADR-0056](https://iqvo.github.io/fulfillment-execution/docs/adr/0056-ship-in-own-container)).** With `shipInOwnContainer: true` and the order line's `lineQuantity` (in eaches), a line that is exactly one full active CASE of its SKU (`lineQuantity` equal to the `unitsPerPack` of the SKU's active CASE level in the local pack-level copy of product-master's events) is sealed in the case itself: the package carries `containerSource: CASE` and the case's GTIN, dimensions and weight in `container`, with no cartonisation. `contents` must then name exactly one SKU. Anything else is refused with `422` and nothing is sealed: not exactly one line (`ship-in-own-container-not-single-line`), a quantity other than one full case (`ship-in-own-container-quantity-mismatch`), no CASE level for the SKU (`ship-in-own-container-no-case-level`), a retired CASE level (`ship-in-own-container-case-retired`), or a case declared without dimensions and weight (`ship-in-own-container-case-dimensions-unknown`). Without the new fields the request and the response are exactly as before.
